page: Amazon Web Services c6g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture, it features 64 dedicated physical cores using the Neoverse-N1 model running at 2.5 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps. No GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 97056.55 and a high software compilation score of 42910.0 in Geekbench. Cached read-only memory bandwidth is exceptionally high at 3782.53 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics are relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 970.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 20.33 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory operations and multi-threaded decompression fall into the average tier.

Given the high physical core count and strong multi-threaded execution, this instance is suited for parallelized workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and high-throughput Redis key-value stores, where it achieved 77.68 million operations per second. Conversely, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds drop to 2.74 tokens per second for 70B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Graviton architecture offers a high density of dedicated physical cores per unit of memory, making it a viable alternative to x86 platforms for highly parallelized, non-vectorized computing tasks.
